key_insight: An unfitted hybrid high-order method can accurately simulate elastodynamic wave propagation across an imperfect slipping interface without aligning the mesh to the interface.
engineering_relevance: The method is robust for solid mechanics problems with unresolved internal interfaces, making it attractive for wave propagation and interface-dominated simulations in complex geometries.
method: Uses an unfitted HHO discretization with doubled unknowns in cut cells and cell agglomeration to handle small cuts.
Reconstructs symmetric strain locally in each cut subcell and enforces the imperfect interface through a regularized stiffness matrix.
Adds interface stabilization and couples the semi-discrete scheme with Newmark or high-order SDIRK time integration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal convergence in 2D tests, robustness over sixteen orders of magnitude in compliancy, and accurate wave transmission across the slipping interface for k=1,2,3.
watch_item: Performance and implementation may be sensitive to interface-cut geometry and the agglomeration/stabilization choices, especially in highly fragmented cut cells.
paper_title: An Unfitted Hybrid High-Order Method for the Elastodynamics Problem with Imperfect Interface
